newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks soar one percent to record close.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks soar one percent to record close.

text.p: Toronto stocks hit new highs on Monday, as investors continued to gobble up Canadian bank stocks and Wall Street turned in a strong session.
The TSE 300 Composite Index jumped 64.48 points, or 1.03 percent, to close at 6332.87 -- its 12th record finish of 1997. The key index also set an intraday high of 6333.27.
Trading was brisk with 85.3 million shares changing hands worth C$1.41 billion ($1.02 billion).
"In Toronto, the banks continued their Friday performance. They were very, very strong," said Rolie Bradley, an institutional salesman with Maison Placements Canada Inc.
The TSE's financial services group closed up 2.05 percent at 6575.29, a few points shy of its all-time high of 6582.53 hit earlier in the session.
The heayweight group led the overall market to new highs on Friday after recent record first quarter profits from Canada big six banks.
Financial services, gold, base metals and consumer products led 12 of 14 sub-groups higher. There were modest losses in conglomerates and real estate.
"New York was up as well which helped push Toronto," Bradley said. The Dow Jones average rose 78 points on Monday.
* Among the banks, Toronto-Dominion Bank jumped 1.25 to close at 40.45, a 52-week high, on 2.06 million shares.
Royal Bank of Canada gained 1.45 to 62.05 1.7 million shares, after earlier reaching a 52-week peak of 62.20.
Bank of Montreal added 1.70 to end at 55.40 on 1.5 million shares. The stock earlier hit a new high of 55.50.
* Potash Corp. of Saskatchewan Inc. rose 1.50 to 107.50 after a U.S. brokerage reinitiated coverage with a buy rating.
* Inco Ltd. was the top base metal gainer, closing up 1.60 at 51.30 on 730,000 shares.
